title: The Hotdish Accords
logline: Judy Eriksen flies in for Marshall's birthday with her hotdish on her lap, just as Lily makes her first one with cream of chicken, and two polite words start a five-day cold war fought in casseroles. Marshall can't refuse a single bite, so Ted, Robin and Barney become his secret stomachs, until Ted calls a blind-tasting summit on the roof.
coldOpen: Kids, in the spring of 2012, your Aunt Lily and Marshall's mother fought a war. It lasted five days, it was fought entirely with casseroles, and your Uncle Marshall gained eleven pounds.

couch.line: Eleven pounds in five days? That's the coolest thing anyone's ever done in one of your stories.
He'll be thrilled to hear that, Luke. He's still trying to lose them.

scenes.summary: Lily has made Marshall's birthday hotdish for the first time, with improvements. Judy arrives unannounced with hers on her lap. One bite, two words: that's different. Marshall explains it's a declaration of war, eats both, and the button is early breakfast.

beats.line: It was Marshall's birthday, and Lily had been in the kitchen since noon.
For thirty-three years, Judy has made Marshall's birthday hotdish. This year, an Aldrin makes it.
I've been too scared to ask for nine years. What is a hotdish?
Technically, a casserole. Bound with canned soup, and capped with a structural layer of tater tots.
Ted, you just described a casserole like it needs a building permit.
Robin, hotdish is how Minnesotans say I love you. We'd never say it out loud. That's how people get hurt.
And this year, I made a few tiny improvements.
Improvements?
Cream of chicken instead of cream of mushroom.
Okay.
A little smoked gouda.
Mm-hmm.
And I laid the tots in a herringbone.
Herringbone! Lily, that's gorgeous.
Ted, you're blushing at a potato.
Lilypad, it's perfect. And since Mom couldn't make it this year, nobody ever has to know.
Happy birthday, sweetie!
Mom! You said you couldn't come!
I said I couldn't come Tuesday, honey. It's Wednesday.
Don't worry, I brought the hotdish. It flew in on my lap. A flight attendant tried to stow it. Once.
Oh! Judy. I actually made one this year. I thought I'd give you the night off.
Oh, honey, that's so sweet. I've never needed a night off.
Well, look at that. You put the tots in a pattern.
It's a herringbone.
Like a floor.
Let me just have one little bite.
Cream of chicken. Well. That's different.
What? Different's fine. Different's nice.
Robin, in Minnesota, that's different is how we declare war.
She said it about my cousin Kyle's fiancée. Two years later, Mom brought a hotdish to the divorce.
Thank you, Judy! I'll take that as a compliment.
You do that, honey.
Sit, sweetie. You'll have mine first. It's your birthday hotdish.
Or mine first. Because it's your birthday.
I'll have both. At the same time. Like a dad who loves all his kids equally.
Honey, nobody loves their kids equally. Ask Marcus.
Two women. One man. Casseroles at dawn. Ted, this is the sexiest thing that's ever happened in this apartment.
Barney, I live here.
I know.
Mom, it's perfect.
Lily, it's perfect.
Which one is more perfect?
Well. I'm here till Sunday, so I'll make breakfast.
Oh, I've got breakfast, Judy.
Then I'll make early breakfast.
Ted. There's an early breakfast now.

scenes.summary: Montage of the cold war: breakfasts and lunches stacked on top of each other. At MacLaren's, Marshall explains the Eriksen clean-plate code and recruits Ted, Robin and Barney as secret stomachs. Robin is in instantly, Ted wants tasting notes, Barney refuses until he meets scotcheroos and Snickers salad.

beats.line: And so began the Hotdish Cold War.
Early breakfast, honey! Eleven pancakes. One for every year you've lived out here.
Regular breakfast! Twelve pancakes. I didn't count. It's twelve.
Lunch for my lawyer! And a meatloaf for your boss, so he's nice to you.
Surprise! Second lunch!
I love lunch.
By Friday, Marshall had eaten nineteen meals in two days. Every one of them was a love letter. And a threat.
Ted, I can't feel my legs. I think my legs are full.
Marshall, just tell them you're full.
Ted, an Eriksen does not leave food on a plate.
My grandpa once cleared an entire funeral buffet. He didn't know the deceased. He just couldn't watch it go to waste.
So he crashed a funeral.
He honored a stranger, Robin. He went back for the ham.
And if one pan comes back with food in it, that woman loses. I can't let either of them lose.
One of them gave me life. The other one could end it.
So I need a team. Of stomachs. Every pan comes back clean, and nobody can ever know.
I'm in.
That fast?
Ted, I'm Canadian. We eat like there's a blizzard tomorrow. There's always a blizzard tomorrow.
I'm in too, but I'm keeping tasting notes. Hotdish is the vernacular architecture of the Upper Midwest.
It's tater tots, Ted.
Count me out. I don't eat from pans. I eat off tiny plates, with a dot of sauce, served by Paolo.
Barney, my mom made scotcheroos.
There's scotch in them?
No.
Then why would you call them that?
Peanut butter rice cereal bars, with a melted chocolate and butterscotch roof.
Marshall, that's children's food. I'm a grown man in a seven-thousand-dollar suit.
Just try one.
Why has nobody told the coasts?
Fine. I'm in. For the bars. Strictly the bars.
There's also Snickers salad.
A salad. With Snickers in it.
And apples. For health.
Minnesota, you beautiful liar.

scenes.summary: The clean pans backfire: both women escalate. In the soup aisle, Judy needles Lily's gouda and Lily fires back with 'that's different'. Marshall imagines admitting he's full (they unite over his deathbed). Ted calls a blind-tasting summit on the roof: winner makes the birthday hotdish forever. Robin turns up as an 'impartial' judge.

beats.line: The plan worked perfectly. Every pan came back clean. Which was the worst thing that could have happened.
Two clean pans yesterday, sweetie! I knew you missed real food.
He cleaned both of mine too, Judy. He licked the spoon.
Then today I'm making three.
Then I'm making four.
Marshall, the team is at capacity. Barney ate a whole hotdish in the stairwell this morning. Standing up. Like a horse.
Oh, smoked gouda. Fancy. Marvin had a fancy phase in the eighties. We got him through it.
And all that cream of mushroom, Judy. That's so... different.
Marshall. Did you teach her that?
Spousal privilege, Mom!
Well. I'll pray on that.
End this. Just tell them you're full.
Ted, you don't know what happens when an Eriksen says he's full.
Mom. Lily. I'm full.
Full?
Lily, call an ambulance.
I'll call Marvin.
I'll call Pastor Lindgren.
I'll start a hotdish for the funeral.
Oh, Lily. That's exactly what I would do.
You're finally getting along. And I'm dying.
Marshall, they got along in that one.
Ted, I died.
Still. Progress.
Ladies! What this war needs is neutral ground.
Tonight. The roof. A blind tasting before three impartial judges.
And the winner?
Makes Marshall's birthday hotdish. Forever.
Fine by me, Judy.
Fine by me, honey.
Pick up more gouda, dear. You'll want it for your fancy phase.
The Hotdish Accords. I've waited my whole life to broker a treaty.
Ted, now they're both making their best one ever. You just ordered two more hotdishes.
Ted, I just passed Judy and Lily on the sidewalk. They were both smiling. I've never been so scared.
Robin! Great news. You're an impartial judge.
Impartial? Ted, I've eaten eleven of Judy's pans and nine of Lily's. I'm not impartial. I'm forty percent hotdish.

scenes.summary: The summit. Ted reads the Accords, Barney arrives in a suit with a secret elastic waist, and the blind tasting lasts one sentence before Robin identifies both pans. The secret stomachs are exposed; Judy knew all along (the corners). Lily demands a verdict and Marshall finally says no: he's full. Judy and Lily rush to him with the exact same instincts, then find out they're both outsiders who married into the hotdish. Judy asks for Lily's recipe: different, the good kind. Future Ted reveals what's on the card.

beats.line: Welcome to the Hotdish Accords. Please note Article eleven.
beats.title: The Hotdish Accords

beats.line: Article eleven is personal, Ted.
Robin, you ate the corners. Nobody eats the corners.
Before we begin, let the record show I am wearing the Surrender.
The what?
A custom suit with a hidden elastic waist. My tailor wept as he sewed it. He called it the death of Milan.
Dish A, please.
A bold mushroom base. A rigorous grid of tots. Very Mies van der Rohe.
Dish A is Judy's. Dish B is Lily's. It's got gouda, and it's laid like a floor.
Robin, honey. How would you know that? It's blind.
Lucky guess.
Very lucky! We've never eaten either one! Not one of the twenty pans!
Marshall. Have they been eating your food?
Define eating.
Oh, I've known since Thursday.
You knew?
My son has never once cleaned the corners of a pan. Those corners were scraped. By a professional.
Thank you.
Then why did you keep cooking more?
A good cook always knows who's eating her food, Lily.
That's it. Marshall, taste them both and tell her which one is better. Right now.
Yes, sweetie. Tell her.
No.
I'm full. I've been full since Wednesday. I'm full in places I didn't know I had places.
Full?
Lily, check his forehead.
Already on it. Back of the hand.
Back of the hand. The front is for amateurs.
That's what I always say.
Ted, look. It's happening. Just like I pictured it.
Marshall, they're getting along!
And I'm not even dead!
Judy, I'm sorry. I didn't want to beat you. I just wanted to be in the recipe.
The recipe?
You Eriksens have a dish for everything. Birthdays, funerals, Tuesdays. The Aldrin family recipe is the number for a Szechuan place.
I just wanted to make him one thing he'd remember the way he remembers yours.
Honey. I'm from Duluth.
My first year, I made Marvin's birthday hotdish. I switched his mother's cream of celery to cream of mushroom.
What did she say?
That's different.
She didn't speak to me until the ice went out on the lake. Then she asked me for the recipe.
Because she liked it?
Because Marvin loved it. Which is why I'm going to need yours written down.
Really? With the chicken?
It's different, honey. I mean the good kind.
Nobody's born into this family, Lily. Well, the Eriksens are. But they can't cook.
Hey!
Beautiful. Very moving. Is anyone finishing Dish B? Because I'm wearing the Surrender.
Kids, from then on, Marshall got two birthday hotdishes every year. He ate both. Your Aunt Robin ate the corners.
Lily still keeps the card Judy wrote that night. At the top: Lily's Hotdish. At the bottom, very small: use mushroom.
